issues.legal_issue: Under a compromise award providing for a property sale, the seller was required to initiate execution of the sale deed, after which the purchaser was to pay the agreed consideration.
material_facts: A decree for possession had been passed before the parties settled their dispute through a Lok Adalat award.

The award provided for the property to be sold to the purchaser or a nominee within a specified period on payment of the agreed consideration, and provided for execution through court if the seller defaulted.
The seller did not execute the sale deed despite requests, while the purchaser sent notices stating that he was ready and willing to pay and later deposited the consideration in court.
issues.conclusion: The seller was required to evince willingness and take the initiative to execute the sale deed; the purchaser had performed his obligation and could seek execution through court if the seller failed to execute it.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of the compromise award, read in the context of the existing decree and the settlement, placed the initial obligation to offer execution of the sale deed on the seller. The purchaser's obligation to pay followed that offer; the seller could not rely on the purchaser's failure to deposit the money earlier when the seller had not taken the required initiative.

rule.if: execution_of_compromise_award and award_requires_sale_for_payment and seller_failed_to_initiate_transfer and purchaser_showed_readiness_to_pay

predicates.execution_of_compromise_award: A party sought court execution of a settlement award resolving an ongoing civil dispute.
predicates.award_requires_sale_for_payment: The award required the seller to transfer property in return for the purchaser's payment of agreed consideration.
predicates.seller_failed_to_initiate_transfer: The seller did not offer to execute the transfer document within the period contemplated by the award.
predicates.purchaser_showed_readiness_to_pay: The purchaser communicated readiness to pay and took steps to make the agreed payment.

issues.definition: When a party seeks execution of a settlement award requiring a sale for payment, and the seller has not initiated the transfer while the purchaser has shown readiness to pay, the purchaser may compel completion of the sale under the award.

issues.legal_issue: A court may extend time and enforce a Lok Adalat award treated as a decree when doing so is appropriate to give effect to the settlement.
material_facts: The parties' dispute was settled by a Lok Adalat award that was to end an appeal and the litigation between them.
The purchaser sought execution after the seller failed to execute the sale deed.
The executing court allowed the purchaser time to deposit the agreed consideration, which he deposited within that time.
The High Court set aside the executing court's order, but the Supreme Court held that the award was deemed a decree and that the court could extend time in an appropriate case.
issues.conclusion: The executing court had jurisdiction to extend the time for deposit and enforce the award; the High Court was wrong to hold otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 21 and 22 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 treat a Lok Adalat award as a decree of a civil court and give courts the powers they have in relation to their own decrees; those powers include extending time in appropriate cases. The award is final and binding under Section 21. The judgment also relied on the principle that a consent judgment is intended to end litigation, as discussed in Sailendra Narayan Bhanja Deo v. State of Orissa, In re South American and Mexican Co., and Kinch v. Walvott; it referred to Order 23 Rule 3 and Section 96(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure in explaining the finality of compromise judgments.

rule.if: execution_of_lok_adalat_award and award_has_time_bound_obligation and party_failed_to_complete_obligation_on_time and extension_would_effectuate_settlement

predicates.execution_of_lok_adalat_award: A party asked a court to enforce an award made by a Lok Adalat.
predicates.award_has_time_bound_obligation: The award required a party to perform an obligation within a specified period.
predicates.party_failed_to_complete_obligation_on_t: A party did not complete the required obligation within the period stated in the award.
predicates.extension_would_effectuate_settlement: Allowing further time would give effect to the settlement rather than defeat it on a technical ground.

issues.definition: If execution of a Lok Adalat award is sought, an obligation was not completed on time, and an extension would effectuate the settlement, the court may extend time and enforce the award.

issues.legal_issue: A notice correctly addressed and returned unclaimed after an attempted delivery and postal intimation may be presumed served without examining the postman.
material_facts: The purchaser sent a lawyer's notice asking the seller to execute the sale deed.
The notice was correctly addressed, an attempt to deliver it was made, and an intimation was left when the seller was absent.
The notice was returned unclaimed, after which the purchaser sent a telegram and a copy of the notice by certificate of posting.
The High Court considered examination of the postman necessary, but the Supreme Court held that it was not.
issues.conclusion: Service could be presumed, and the purchaser was not required to examine the postman to establish service.
issues.legal_principle: The presumption under Section 27 of the Post Office Act applies where a notice is correctly addressed and sent through the post; the presumption under Section 114 of the Evidence Act operates independently. On the facts, the postal endorsement and intimation supported the presumption of service, and the postman did not have to be examined.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and notice_correctly_addressed and delivery_attempted_with_intimation and notice_returned_unclaimed

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party sought court enforcement of an obligation to execute a document.
predicates.notice_correctly_addressed: The sender addressed the notice correctly to the person required to act.
predicates.delivery_attempted_with_intimation: Postal delivery was attempted and an intimation was left when delivery could not be completed.
predicates.notice_returned_unclaimed: The notice was returned without delivery as unclaimed.

issues.definition: In an execution proceeding, a correctly addressed notice returned unclaimed after attempted delivery and postal intimation may be treated as served.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may not set aside an executing court's order by reappraising evidence and misconstruing the settlement award beyond the proper limits of revision.
material_facts: The executing court heard witnesses, considered documentary evidence, and allowed the purchaser time to deposit the consideration.
The purchaser made the deposit within the time allowed by the executing court.
The High Court, exercising revision, reappraised the evidence, misread which party had to initiate execution of the sale deed, and set aside the executing court's order.
The Supreme Court found the High Court's view of the award and its reasoning on the evidence and postal notice incorrect.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's interference was unjustified, and its order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs revisional jurisdiction. The Supreme Court held that the High Court exceeded the proper limits of that jurisdiction by investigating questions of fact and reappraising evidence, and that its interference rested on a mistaken interpretation of the award and the record.

rule.if: revision_against_execution_order and executing_court_considered_evidence and revisional_court_reappraised_facts and revisional_court_misread_settlement_terms

predicates.revision_against_execution_order: A party challenged an executing court's order in revision.
predicates.executing_court_considered_evidence: The executing court heard evidence and considered material produced by the parties before making its order.
predicates.revisional_court_reappraised_facts: The revisional court independently reassessed factual questions and evidence considered by the executing court.
predicates.revisional_court_misread_settlement_term: The revisional court interpreted the parties' settlement as imposing an obligation on a different party than the settlement required.

issues.definition: When revision challenges an execution order based on evidence, a revisional court's reappraisal of facts and misreading of the settlement make its interference unwarranted.
